mission: SNKRDUNK discovery restart (owner priority fix 2026-10-19; snkrdunk collector change allowed for this fix only, delivered by staging-automerge with a collector rollout outside 02:00-06:00 UTC, never hand-merged or native auto-merged). Discovery stopped after the 2026-10-07 canaries 3676/3677 because no code plans a next intent. Each scheduled SNKR turn now plans at most one guarded snkr-published:auto-v1 intent per 6h with the existing adapter bounds (300 requests, 20 products, 12 anchors, radius 1..48), and published discovery re-reads sitemap shards retained within 7 days instead of re-fetching and re-storing them. Staging only; PSA10 OFF; no identity, resolver, mapping, approval, price, Market Value/Index, schedule, budget, variable, schema or yuyutei change.

impacts.reason: Re-enables the already-built published discovery lane by planning it: after recovery and before drain, one pending discovery row via plan_discovery_scope with the cursor the existing intent() validator requires; nothing else is written. Guards (any one skips the turn): an open snkr-published intent; last auto intent < SNKRDUNK_AUTO_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_H (default 6) ago; 2 of last 3 auto intents not completed; budget disabled or paused; next-40-min RAW demand x 24h peak RAW request cost + 300 > unreserved window; no approved manual_verified anchor; last 3 auto intents inspected nothing with an unchanged anchor pool. Kill switch SNKRDUNK_AUTO_DISCOVERY (default true, no variable change needed). Planner errors are logged and the RAW turn continues; lock loss still propagates.

Shard reuse: an advertised shard whose 200 response this parser retained within 7 days is re-read from that raw_snapshot (base64 envelope, SHA-256 checked) and recorded in the cursor with reused=true; otherwise fetched and retained as before. Robots and the index are always fetched and robots still gates every shard. Same exclusions, neighbour order, product bounds, fences and candidate-only writes.

Real-PostgreSQL planner tests (planned claim accepted by intent(), open intent, interval, rotation, closed/short budget, failures, exhausted neighbourhoods, kill switch, planner error); shard reuse and refusal of old/tampered/other-parser/failed shards. Test conftests default the kill switch off so existing scheduled-turn tests keep their behaviour.
Documents automatic planning, its guards, shard reuse and how to stop it.

resources.name: Staging Postgres (no migration; freshness_work discovery rows, raw_snapshots and snkrdunk_candidates only)

routes: Existing scheduled snkrdunk-due turns (27,57 * * * *) claim the planned intent under existing admission; no new endpoint, schedule or manual run
dependencies: published discovery adapter from PR #70 (unchanged bounds); freshness queue and admission unchanged; source_dispatch_budgets unchanged
impact.deployment_impact: Only the snkrdunk collector is rolled out (yuyutei shards untouched). At most 4 intents/day, each reserved at 300 requests (MEASURED canaries: 199 requests for 2 intents). ESTIMATE about 100 requests and 0.2 MB stored per run after shards are retained once per 7 days (about 9 MB, MEASURED 18.4 MB for the 2 canaries), about 2 MB/day in total. New rows are unmatched candidates only; no mapping, price or approval.

recovery.procedure: Automatic during rollout: snkrdunk-collector restored to its verified a504e47 deployment (collector_services recovery_deployment_id). After delivery: a native revert PR delivered by staging-automerge with a snkrdunk rollout. An intent already planned is a normal bounded explicit intent that the previous code also runs, or is settled with the zero-request rollback in SNKR_PUBLISHED_DISCOVERY_RECOVERY.md. Retained RAW and unmatched candidates stay as evidence.
recovery.trigger: any source denial, 403/429 or challenge on a discovery request; any price, mapping or approval write from discovery; more than 4 auto intents in 24h; a RAW refresh backlog caused by discovery reservations; storage growth above 5 MB/day attributable to snkr-published-discovery-v1; deployment failure; schedule, variable or budget drift.
recovery.backup: Not applicable: no schema or existing-row change; additive rows only. Railway Postgres daily backups continue.

verification.observation_window: Delivery artifact, then the first scheduled snkrdunk-due turn on the merge plans one auto-v1 intent (or logs a skip reason) and the next turns claim and complete it. Over 24h: at most 4 auto intents, each completed with inspected identities and only unmatched candidates; 0 price/mapping writes; no source pause; RAW refresh not_blocked_deficit stays 0; snkr-published storage within estimate (snkrdunk-discovery-state diagnostic once PR #177 is merged).

operational_notes: Identity-capture batches were paused 2026-10-17 15:41Z to 2026-10-18 13:57Z (owner decisions). They are RESUMED as before: each enqueue-remaining-50 ops-write batch is still dispatched as a dry run first and approved by the owner in the staging-ops Environment. Capture-day storage cuts (options A to G) are not built: the remaining backlog is about 300 MB one-off against 2,825 MB room.
D9 F2 (about 220 prints waiting on capture intents or captures) is no longer stalled; it proceeds with the resumed batches.

Storage watch (owner 2026-10-18): every storage check reports days until the 3 GiB reserve (room_to_reserve_mb_s9 divided by the current growth rate) and flags the owner when it drops below 45 days, to plan retention or a bigger volume.

F1 go-live: about 762 exact proposals from this rule go live only in owner-approved ops-write approve-f1-batch runs of about 500 (dry run first, apply pinned to its SHA-256), with a 48 h storage check after each.

verification.observation_window: After merge: one fleet-vs-receipt run with the default chain reports all_match true for 10 collectors; one approve-f1-batch dry run (owner-approved in staging-ops) completes with status ok, batch_size about 500 and no excluded reason the owner did not expect; batch 1 apply only after the owner reviews it, then a 48 h storage check.
